email.body1:
Parker, saw Anaqua acquired Patrix, adding nearly 400 IP management customers and a bigger European and law-firm footprint.

A deal that size usually creates a much larger account map than the inside team can cover before momentum fades. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Anaqua off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Parker, quick follow-up for Anaqua.

After an acquisition, cross-sell and expansion targets usually jump faster than headcount can. Most inside teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book against the combined base, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your inside team needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Parker, last bit of proof for Anaqua.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Anaqua's reply rate likely compares to other IP software vendors. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Parker, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling inside-sales coverage without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Integrating an acquisition is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to an inside-sales IP motion? I'll tailor it to Anaqua either way.
